artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1732: The Council of the Gods
artworks.artist: Giovanni Battista Sintes, after Nicola Michetti
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows a busy square with an ornate building in the background. The building has a domed structure and a detailed facade. Figures are spread across the square, some talking or moving. In the center, there is a cloud-like formation supporting a smaller domed structure with figures inside and around it. The scene is depicted with detailed line work characteristic of engraving. The color scheme is monochrome. Additional architectural elements are visible in the background.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1738: Allegory of Regal Providence
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a mythical scene with numerous figures and a chariot. The detailed artwork depicts a grand mythological scene in which a chariot led by lions and a regal figure is positioned in the sky, surrounded by clouds and other mythical characters playing instruments. Below, there are various figures engaged in dynamic poses, some working with tools or instruments and others interacting, amidst a rocky, mountainous terrain. To the left, more individuals appear in industrious action, using tools, while below them, figures with horses suggest further motion. The detailed etching showcases fine line work, creating a sense of movement and drama through the composition.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1738: The Triumph of Bacchus and Ceres
artworks.artist: Miguel de Sorellò, after Carl Marcus Tuscher
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is an engraving of various figures engaged in a grand vignette. The scene is rich with characters and symbols. There is a central figure on a chariot surrounded by others engaged in activity. The image features a densely packed composition with figures in classical garments, some holding instruments or weapons. In the lower central area and sides, there are figures with water-themed elements. This is in the style of an allegorical or mythological engraving typical of the late Baroque period.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1741: Allegory of Regal Magnificence
artworks.artist: Miguel de Sorellò, after François Hutin
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of allegorical figures arranged in a complex scene with classical elements. The scene includes ethereal figures among clouds and earthly elements. The figures above are depicted with wings and holding various symbols such as a mirror and a staff. Below, figures are shown seated or standing in contemplative poses, alongside a reclining lion, a wheel symbolizing time or fortune, drapery, and flaglike devices. The drawing is detailed with cross-hatching shading techniques for depth and texture in a monochrome composition.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1741: Neptune and Amphitrite
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring Neptune and Amphitrite accompanied by mythological figures and a chariot in the sky. A lighthouse with intricate detailing is positioned in the background on top of a large structure. The foreground includes deities and mythical beings engaged in various activities. The scene includes dynamic postures and symbolic elements indicative of a narrative context.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1742: The Contest of Neptune and Minerva
artworks.artist: Miguel de Sorellò, after François Hutin
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring mythological elements and a dynamic composition. The drawing illustrates a scene with multiple figures, including a group of seated individuals on clouds, several standing figures, winged entities, equestrians, and animals. The central focus is an interaction between these figures, characterized by dramatic gestures and expressions. The composition is rich with movement, as a horse rears up, and various people demonstrate animated poses. The background includes architectural elements and swirling clouds, creating depth. The detailed linework highlights the expressions and musculature of the figures. There is text at the bottom.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1742: Ulysses and the Sirens
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a maritime scene. It features a large wooden ship in rough waters with mythical creatures resembling mermaids or sirens. Some creatures are on rocks, while others are in the water. Two individuals on the ship interact with the creatures, with other crew members visible. The ship's sails billow under a dark sky. The drawing is detailed with cross-hatching and fine lines, and includes an Italian inscription at the bottom.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1743: Venus Genetrix
artworks.artist: Miguel de Sorellò, after François Hutin
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an assembly of classical figures in a celestial and underwater setting. The artwork illustrates a gathering of mythological deities and creatures, set against an expansive backdrop of clouds and waves. In the upper part of the image, several figures recline on clouds, including a central figure holding a set of compasses, and another pouring liquid from a large vessel. Other figures seem to be observing or engaging in activities. Below, there are mermaids or sea creatures emerging from the ocean, gathered around a reclining figure with a large shell above their head. The scene is executed with intricate detail, highlighting the flowing drapery and dynamic movement of the figures. The drawing also contains a richly detailed border and an inscription at the bottom.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1743: The Royal Hunt
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a hunting scene. The image depicts a group of clothed figures engaged in hunting, with some on foot and others on elephants. The setting is a forested area with trees and hills in the background. In the foreground, there are animals, including a deer and other hunted game. The figures are wearing classical attire, some holding spears and showing action and movement. The scene is detailed with intricate line work, capturing motion and the natural environment.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1745: Triumphal Arch for the Return of King Charles of Bourbon to Naples
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows a neoclassical architectural structure viewed from a straight-on perspective. The horizon is low in the composition, aligned with the base of the archway at the center. Various statues adorn the structure. The brushstrokes and line work are precise and detailed, akin to an engraving or etching. The color palette is dominated by sepia tones. Figures and horses closest to us suggest motion. Additional architecture can be seen beyond the main archway.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1746: The Territories of the Kingdom of Naples
artworks.artist: Miguel de Sorellò, after Francisco Preciado de la Vega
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an architectural facade. The image shows an intricately designed building facade with classical elements such as columns, arches, and niches with statues. Above the central archway is a large emblem with statues of angels on each side. The facade includes ornamental cornices and sculptural decorations. In the foreground, there are figures interacting, potentially involved in a ceremonial or communal activity. The drawing demonstrates careful detail and shading to add depth to the architectural features.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1750: The New Pier of Naples
artworks.artist: Jérôme Charles Bellicard, after Michelangelo Specchi (architect)
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image is taken at sea level, displaying a grand structure at the center. The horizon is low with docked ships on a pier. Ships extend into the distance on the right. The etching is detailed, capturing architectural elements and patterns. The color palette is monochromatic, depicting shadows and lines for textures. Water, a small boat, and crowds are visible. The sky is lightly shaded with clouds in the background.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1751: Triumphal Arch for Roger I of Sicily
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an architectural monument with a central equestrian statue. The image depicts an elaborate edifice with towering columns and decorative sculptures, showcasing an intricate architectural design. The central feature is a statue of a rider on horseback, positioned on a pedestal under a grand arch. The composition includes symmetrical stairs on either side leading up to the platform where the statue stands. Ornamental elements, such as winged figures sitting atop the arch and crowned emblems, add to the grandeur of the scene. Lifelike statues are placed atop the columns and amidst various figures portrayed at different levels, creating a sense of depth and scale. This artistic rendition reflects a classical style with attention to detail, space, and proportion, suggesting ceremonial or monumental themes.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1751: The Palace of Wisdom, Studies, and the Sciences
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image showcases a grand, multi-tiered architectural structure adorned with sculptures and intricate decoration. The composition focuses on the elevation of the building, with sculptures and figures on each level culminating in a dynamic sculptural group at the top. The etching style emphasizes detailed textures and shading, depicting stone and draped figures. The color palette is monochromatic, featuring sepia and dark tones typical of engravings. Figures are shown on the stairs and throughout the building, offering scale and activity. Classical elements like columns, arches, and balustrades add decorative elegance.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1752: A "Deliziosa" Alluding to Villa Carl'Amalia in Caserta
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows an architectural drawing of a symmetrical courtyard scene from a slightly elevated point of view. The composition is centered around an ornate column topped with a statue. The horizon is implied by the base of the architectural structures and the ground plane, lined with arches and decorated obelisks on both sides. The style of the piece is indicative of intricate line work, consistent with 18th-century etching techniques, showcasing fine details in the stonework and embellishments. The color palette is monochromatic, rendered in shades of sepia and light brown. Several human figures and a horse-drawn carriage are scattered throughout the scene, adding a sense of scale and activity. In the distance, the structures rise in complexity, framed by soft clouds.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1752: The Banquet of the Gods in Villa Carl'Amalia in Caserta
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows a symmetrical, classical architectural scene. The main feature is an elaborate triumphal structure with a frontal perspective. A grand staircase defines the horizon with figures in the lower part. At the center is a tall column with a statue, surrounded by draperies, urns, and sculptures. People are walking in the foreground. The sky has light, linear clouds on a clear day. The color scheme is white and brown, resembling a traditional engraving or etching style, focusing on details and linework.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1754: The Palace of Venus in Cyprus
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image displays an ornate architectural structure that resembles a classical facade, possibly a palace or grand pavilion. The horizon line is not defined, as the structure dominates the composition. A grand artistic ornament tops the building, surrounded by swirling cloud-like forms. The artwork features intricate line work reminiscent of engraving, creating depth and texture across elements such as statues and stone masonry. The color palette is monochromatic using shades of gray to emphasize the engraving technique, highlighting architectural details through shadows and highlights. Figures engaged in social interaction and leisurely activities populate the foreground, leading the eye up tiered steps towards the entrance. Symmetrical gardens and carved urns in the distance frame the building, adding balance and grandeur.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1754: An Allegory of Waterworks
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows a detailed architectural structure, potentially a fountain or monument, viewed from a slightly elevated angle. The horizon line is towards the middle of the composition, with two tall obelisks flanking the main structure. The structure is intricate, with fine linework and brushstrokes resembling classical etching or engraving. The color palette is monochromatic, predominantly sepia tones. People in period clothing are scattered around, providing scale. Delicate clouds fill the sky in the background.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1755: A Triumphal Bridge with Antiquities from Herculaneum
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an elaborate architectural scene with a triumphal bridge. The image depicts a grandiose structure featuring a bridge composed of multiple arches, with decorative elements like columns and statues. Atop the central arch, there are sculptures, including a figure triumphant, while on either end of the bridge, statues of elephants are perched upon pedestals, carrying flags. Below the bridge, figures are seen in small boats on the water, and a carriage is drawn by horses. The scene is set in a classical architectural style with ornate detailing and numerous flags and fine carvings. The lower section of the image contains an inscription in Italian text.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1755: A Royal Hunting Lodge
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows an elaborate architectural structure with a frontal and slightly elevated view. The building features a dramatic water feature at its center, including an ornate fountain erupting skyward. Symmetrical staircases lead up to the building, flanked by additional fountains. The fine and detailed brushstrokes or etching lines capture the baroque grandeur of the architecture. The color palette is monochromatic, with varying shades of sepia. Small figures are seen in motion or gathering near the building, while the structure dominates the composition.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1756: A Triumphal Arch between Mount Etna and Mount Vesuvius
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a triumphal arch set against a volcanic landscape. The scene depicts an elaborate archway adorned with classical sculptures and intricate details, situated between two volcanic mountains with smoke rising from their peaks. The architectural structure includes figures on horseback at the top, flanked by scrollwork and decorative embellishments. Small human figures and animals are depicted beneath the archway and in the surrounding open space. The sky is filled with swirling clouds, lending a dramatic backdrop to the composition.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1756: The Temple of Ceres
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows a frontal perspective of a grand architectural structure resembling a monumental archway. The horizon is low, with the structure and landscape stretching across the image. A slightly elevated central area leads up to the arch and statue. The architectural details are highlighted with intricate lines and etching techniques, showcasing a classical style with statues and decorative elements adorning the arch. The color palette is monochromatic, consisting of various shades of sepia or black and white. Closest to us, there is a scene with elegantly dressed figures, horse-drawn carriages, and animals, adding a sense of scale and activity. Beyond this, stairs lead up to the centerpiece where a statue sits prominently within the archway. In the distance on either side of the main structure, small domed pavilions are surrounded by trees and landscaped gardens. The sky is filled with swirling clouds delicately etched above, providing a dramatic backdrop to the architectural focus.

artworks.title: The Prima Macchina for the Chinea of 1757: The Colonnade of the Athenian Lyceum
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Pozzi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an architectural structure with ornate details and classical elements. The drawing depicts a grand, classical portico with multiple columns, an elaborately detailed pediment, and several statues adorning the facade. Flanking the structure are two reclining figures integrated into the landscape. The sky above the structure is depicted using intricate line work, suggesting clouds. Figures involved in pastoral or farm work are depicted in the foreground.

artworks.title: The Seconda Macchina for the Chinea of 1757: The Fortress of Cockaigne
artworks.artist: Giuseppe Pozzi, after Giuseppe Palazzi, after Paolo Posi
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Vincent Buonanno in Honor of Andrew Robison
artworks.description: The image shows an elaborate architectural structure viewed from the front. The horizon is low, with ornate architecture resembling a grand fortress adorned with intricate carvings and sculptures. Flags and banners on top of towers sway gently. People and animals near the structure add scale and activity. Some individuals seem to be part of a procession or gathering. The artwork features meticulous line work and brushstrokes creating depth and texture. The color scheme is mainly sepia, giving an antique look to the scene. In the background, an elaborate fountain structure complements the grand theme.
